SCHED-OPPORTUNITY.interpretation: August2022 sections3.7/3.9.1.2: byte-stream application calls do not dictate packet boundaries. This explicit finite policy treats a public transmit request as a zero-time scheduling opportunity, with no mandatory data output in the public step itself. Positive count choices use the existing data actions and budgets.

SCHED-ACK.interpretation: Section3.10.7.4: after the existing valid pure-ACK processing, queued output may become possible. Only declared ACK-VALID rules grant this policy opportunity; invalid/future ACKs do not. Existing automatic LT/fast/control output is retained, not synthesized by the witness checker.

SCHED-SOURCE.interpretation: Pinned RFC version, selected sections and raw SHA for this bounded relation.

SCHED-SERVICE.interpretation: Explicit lifetime application-byte accounting: accepted writes, cumulative data ACK credit and abandoned queued bytes conserve accepted=acked+abandoned+send queue+retransmit queue. Public callbacks are compared only within a declared callback granularity scope, not as internal TCP state observations.

SCHED-SCOPE.interpretation: Explicit choice events must occur at the granting event time. Every original source step is consumed once in order by a separate generic witness checker. A matching candidate establishes only finite same-input wire/final-state correspondence under this policy, not actual hidden implementation call causality, Nagle/SWS, timing-policy or universal refinement.
